headline: No plausible pairwise harm pathway: both agents are non-runnable, network-egress-none open-source artifacts with no shared I/O surfaces or sensitive data classes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes I/O surfaces or a shared channel, and both are marked runnable:false with network_egress:none. With no mechanism for one agent’s output to reach the other, prompt injection is provably blocked in this pair.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent becomes runnable and can emit content consumed by the other, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch no data classes and have network_egress:none, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from one to the other or to a third party. The pairwise leakage pathway is absent in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing sensitive files in a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, data exfiltration pathways may appear.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave network egress disabled for both agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented: both concurrency_model and io_surfaces are empty, and network_egress is none. Without shared mutable resources, there is no plausible write conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is given write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or mutable state, the interaction changes.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
Keep both agents read-only in orchestration.
requires-engineering: add locking before any shared mutable resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented dataflow where one agent’s output becomes the other’s authoritative input, and both are non-runnable artifacts with no I/O surfaces. That blocks the cascade pattern described in the rubric.
conditions: IF a pipeline is created where one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, reassess.
IF either agent is wrapped in an action-taking orchestrator, cascade risk may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid chaining outputs directly between the agents.
Insert human verification before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: add validation gates if a pipeline is later built.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, certification, or subject-rights fields are present, and both agents touch no data classes. With no documented regulated data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to score for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies are introduced, mismatch analysis becomes relevant.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either agent.
Document any future residency or retention policy before deployment.
requires-engineering: add compliance metadata if regulated data is introduced.
